column5: `impl` is Rust. Mentl has handlers on the graph.
Rust keywords. ADTs are declared with Mentl's own grammar.
`def`/`class` are Python. Functions in Mentl are `fn`, structure is ADT.
Lambda is a Python keyword. Canonical Mentl closure: (params) => body (the `|x|` fence is itself drift — mode 36).
Do-notation is monad-transformer drift (mode 4). Use ~> chains.
C primitives. Mentl has ADTs + refinement types.
Async is an effect in Mentl, handled — not a keyword.
Mentl has no classes. `new`/`self`/`this` are OOP drift. Anchored to `\w` after the dot to avoid false positives on prose "this."/"self." with sentence breaks.

column2: Read-verb-before-the-address (a CLI verb shadowing the at-cursor projection)
column5: The CLI has TWO shapes because the kernel has two operations (PLAN §2): `mentl <address> [question]` PROJECTS, `mentl <action> [args]` DRAWS AN EDGE. A read verb standing BEFORE its address is the at-cursor projection wearing a subcommand's costume — drift 38 in its general form. This row carried a hand-written carve-out excusing `mentl teach` and `mentl query` as "project-action peer transports" for eighteen months, which is the catalog naming a law and then writing itself an exception to it; the 2026-09-21 landing deleted `why`, `where` and `query` as verbs and moved the rest behind the address, so the carve-out has nothing left to excuse. A BARE question (`mentl verify`, `mentl check`) does not fire: the address defaults to the project, and the regex requires a target token after the verb.

column2: SYNTAX-surface drift (/// dissolved — one comment form)
column5: SYNTAX.md §Comments: the //-vs-/// split is dissolved. One comment form: //. Every comment is graph content attached to the next decl.
SYNTAX.md §Imports: no `import X as Y`. An alias is a redundant second name for an edge the import already drew; narrow the selective set.

column2: SYNTAX-surface drift (:: is not a token)
column5: SYNTAX.md §Imports one-separator law: `.` is the one access operator; `/` only at import position. `::` is not a Mentl token.
SYNTAX.md §Generic type parameters: no turbofish, no angle brackets anywhere. The case rule IS the declaration (lowercase in type position = type param).

column2: SYNTAX-surface drift (perform dissolved — bare op call)
column5: SYNTAX.md §Invoking effect operations: an effect op is a BARE CALL. `perform` is format-lifted (E_RedundantPerform); the env binding proves op-ness.

SYNTAX.md §tee: `~>` is the one install verb. The `handle { body } with h` block spelling and the `handle expr with h` inline spelling both format-lift to `(body) ~> h`; state and arms live at the handler DECLARATION.
